title: Admin Slate: compact service account & permissions UX grooming
content:
Context and goals:
- Problem: support teams want a compact admin surface for day-to-day access management (create service account, rotate keys, view last usage) without drilling into full org settings. Current console flows are too many clicks for common tasks.
- Goal: design a compact ‘Admin Slate’ panel on Org -> Teams that surfaces quick actions, service account lifecycle, key telemetry, and an audit log summary card. Keep it low-friction for SREs and platform engineers.

Audience and constraints:
- Primary: platform engineers, infra SREs, security reviewers.
- Must play nicely with Dedicated/Private deployment RBAC semantics (some features disabled for Private).
- Must not expose raw secret material in logs or UIs. Key material only shown once on creation with clear copy about copy-store.

High-level proposal (wireframe writeup):
1) Admin Slate header (compact)
   - Title: Team / Org name + small role badge counts (Admins = 2, Editors = 5, Viewers = 24)
   - Quick actions row: "Invite member" (modal), "Create service account" (quick flow), "Rotate org keys" (managed workflow)
   - Small gear overflow: access settings, elevated audit, role templates

2) Service account mini-card (left column) - repeatable list item
   - Row content: SA name, short description, last-used: 3h, active keys: 1, created: 2025-03-12
   - Inline actions (icon-only): copy cred, rotate key, deactivate, view audit timeline
   - Click to expand -> right-side panel with richer lifecycle UI (history, associated routes, allowed models)

3) API Keys & secrets area (center column)
   - Top: "Active keys (count)" summary with token usage this week (tokens/day sparkline)
   - Key item: masked id, created_by, scope (routes/models), last_seen, usage_heat (low/med/high)
   - Danger zone affordance: show "revoke all" + cooldown and impact preview modal (simulate which services would fail)

4) Permissions matrix snapshot (bottom / collapsed)
   - Tiny matrix: top row roles, left column resources (models, routes, billing, infra). Hover details in tooltip.
   - Link: "Open full RBAC editor" (navigates to policy editor)

5) Audit log summary card (right column)
   - Show last 3 critical events (revoke, permission-change, failed-auth) with relative times and actor avatars
   - Filters: quick toggles for "critical", "service-account", "api-key"
   - Lightweight search box with regex-ish token (advanced opens full audit view)
   - CTA: "Export last 90d" (CSV/JSON)

Wireframe specifics / interaction notes:
- Compactness rules: all top-level actions must be reachable within two clicks from the top-level org/team list.
- Create service account quick flow (1 modal): name -> optional description -> role template dropdown -> create -> show credential modal (copy-once) -> async creation + toast -> post-create: telemetry snippet with sample curl and targeted route URL.
- Rotate key: open mini modal with preview of affected routes and expected fail rate (computed from recent last_seen), option to create rotated key and schedule deprecation (30d)
- Copy cred button shows ephemeral toast "Copied — secrets never stored; download .json now? [Download] [Close]"

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- AC1: Create service account flow completes and returns a single view-only credential string which can be downloaded once.
- AC2: Admin Slate lists all service accounts for the team and shows last_seen and active keys in the list.
- AC3: Rotate key flow allows creating a replacement key and scheduling old key deprecation.
- AC4: Audit summary card surfaces at least 3 recent critical events and filters work locally.
- AC5: Quick actions are accessible from team list with <= 2 clicks.

Telemetry & backend needs (notes for eng):
- New small endpoints: /teams/:id/sa-summary (list with last_seen, key_count, last_activity_ts) and /teams/:id/key-usage (7d sparkline).
- Add event types to audit stream: SA_CREATED, SA_ROTATED, API_KEY_REVOKED, PERM_ASSIGN.
- Cardinality concern: last_seen per-key per-route could explode. Proposed approach: sample per-day aggregation on write side and only expose top-5 hotspots in UI.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Q1: For Private (on-prem) installs, can we show token usage sparkline without shipping telemetry out? (likely no; show local-only aggregated numbers and mark as "private metrics").
- Q2: Should role-templates be editable inline or require separate editor? Tradeoff: faster but risk inconsistent templates.
- Q3: UX for simultaneous rotation across multiple SAs — do we batch or force single-SA flow?
- Q4: How to represent cross-team service accounts (shared SAs) in matrix? show in both teams with label "shared"?

Backlog (rough prioritization):
- P0: Implement SA list + create quick modal + copy-once credential modal (JIRA: PLAT-887).
- P0: Add audit summary card + backend event types.
- P1: Rotate key UI with schedule deprecation and impact preview (depends on key-usage endpoint).
- P1: API key revoke all with impact simulation modal.
- P2: Compact permissions snapshot + link to full RBAC editor.
- P2: Role template inline edits with audit trail.

Design artifacts to produce:
- Low-fi wireframes (3 screens): Admin Slate collapsed, SA expanded panel, Create SA modal. Sketch notes attached to PR above.
- Hi-fi mocks for desktop and narrow tablet.
- Microcopy doc: credential copy modal + danger modal content.

Security & compliance notes:
- Never render raw secret in audit logs or in persistent UI. Credential shown exactly once at creation.
- When exporting audit logs, scrub secret tokens and only include key IDs.
- Include event-level actor_id and request_ip for compliance exports.

UX anti-patterns to avoid:
- Showing full key lists without masking.
- Burying rotate/revoke behind >3 clicks.
- Using modal chains requiring repeated credential display.

Prototype test plan (5-person usability quick test):
- Tasks: create SA, copy credential, schedule key rotation, view audit entry for rotation, simulate revoke and view impacted routes.
- Success metric: task completion >= 90% and average time to create SA < 70s.

Notes to reviewers (what I want feedback on):
- Is the sparkline + last_seen enough to make a confident rotate decision? What else would you need?
- Does the compact matrix give enough context to avoid navigating to full RBAC editor?
- Thoughts on export formats for audit (csv vs json with nested actor fields)?

Misc / scratch thoughts (raw):
- Consider an "automation API key" template that limits to rerank/embeddings routes only (low blast radius).
- Could show "used-by" sample services under each SA (top-3) based on route-level last_seen aggregation.
- Danger modal should include a simulated list of customers/routes impacted (anonymized) — could help product before hitting revoke-all.

Next steps and owners:
- Design: create low-fi wireframes (Maya) by 2026-03-10.
- Backend: add summary endpoints and audit event types (Samir) sprint 23.
- PM: scope rotate/schedule and acceptance testcases (Priya) by next planning.

References and quick links:
- Existing RBAC editor spec: CONFLUENCE-UI-1102
- Audit ingestion backlog: JIRA-SYS-412
- Console PR with previous SA UX: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/614
